item.title: Microsoft Patches 973 Bugs as CVE-2026-75650 Adobe Commerce RCE Is Exploited
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Sep 22:00 → 09 Sep 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

“StyleSmuggler” – Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento RCE (CVE-2026-75650): Overview and Takeaways — Must Read

Adobe disclosed a critical unauthenticated RCE flaw, CVE-2026-75650 “StyleSmuggler,” affecting Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source, with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. Organizations should immediately apply Adobe’s VULN-39341 hotfix and treat any internet-exposed unpatched instance since September 4, 2026 as potentially compromised.

  • Adobe disclosed CVE-2026-75650, dubbed “StyleSmuggler,” on September 7, 2026, and assigned it an initial CVSS score of 10.0.
  • The vulnerability affects Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source and allows unauthenticated remote code execution through PHP injection in Magento’s email template engine.
  • Exploitation has been confirmed in the wild since at least September 4, 2026, with attackers deploying a Rust-based Linux backdoor and PHP web shells on compromised storefronts.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-75650 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 8, 2026.
  • The article recommends applying Adobe’s VULN-39341 Composer hotfix, verifying successful installation, checking Sansec’s indicators of compromise, and treating unpatched internet-exposed instances as potentially compromised.

Technologies: cms

Products: adobe-commerce, adobe-commerce-b2b, magento-open-source

Vendors: adobe, magento, sansec, netspi

Microsoft Patch Tuesday for September 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities — Must Read

Microsoft’s September 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 973 vulnerabilities, including 113 critical issues and two Windows elevation-of-privilege flaws already exploited in the wild. Organizations should prioritize applying the updates, especially for the exploited and more-likely-to-be-exploited vulnerabilities, while Talos has released Snort coverage for some exploit attempts.

  • Microsoft released its September 2026 monthly security update addressing 973 vulnerabilities across multiple products, including 113 marked as critical.
  • Microsoft stated that two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-81963 in Windows Update Stack and CVE-2026-85880 in Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call, have been exploited in the wild.
  • Out of the 113 critical vulnerabilities, 82 are remote code execution vulnerabilities.
  • Microsoft assessed several vulnerabilities as more likely to be exploited, including issues affecting Windows Kerberos, Windows Routing and Remote Access Service, Windows Deployment Services, Spring Cloud Azure, Windows DNS Server, Azure Cosmos DB, and other products.
  • Talos released a new Snort ruleset to detect attempts to exploit some of the disclosed vulnerabilities, with coverage listed for both Snort 2 and Snort 3 rules.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access, database, hypervisor, identity-provider, iam, cloud-platform, ids-ips

Microsoft adds age-awareness APIs that can tell if users are children, teens, or adults — May Read

Microsoft is adding Windows 11 APIs that let apps determine whether a user is a child, teen, or adult without exposing their exact birthdate. The system ties into Microsoft Age Verification so users can verify once and let apps apply age-appropriate safeguards, including for AI experiences.

  • Microsoft is adding new age-awareness APIs to Windows 11 that let apps determine whether a user is a child, teenager, or adult without exposing the user's exact date of birth.
  • The Windows Age API can return age ranges including under 10, 10-12, 13-15, 16-17, and 18+ using information associated with a Microsoft account.
  • Developers can use GetUserAgeRangeAsync to retrieve age groups and GetAgeVerificationStatusAsync to check whether a user's age has been verified rather than self-reported.
  • Microsoft says the APIs could let apps automatically adjust features and safeguards for younger users, including in AI experiences, without requiring parents to configure every app individually.
  • Microsoft Age Verification stores a verified age status with a Microsoft account and is already available through Microsoft storefronts in Singapore, Brazil, and Australia, with more regions planned.

Technologies: operating-system, identity-provider

Products: windows-11, windows-age-api, microsoft-age-verification, microsoft-account

Vendors: microsoft

item.title: SAP OVERPASS, Magento StyleSmuggler, Windows Patch Tuesday, and Liquid Bitcoin Theft
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Sep 14:00 → 08 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

StyleSmuggler (CVE-2026-75650): Frequently asked questions about Adobe Commerce and Magento zero-day — Must Read

Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source have a critical unauthenticated RCE zero-day, CVE-2026-75650 “StyleSmuggler,” that was actively exploited before Adobe released a hotfix on September 7, 2026. Affected stores should apply the hotfix immediately and perform incident response, since patching alone will not remove existing compromises.

  • CVE-2026-75650, dubbed StyleSmuggler, is a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability affecting Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source.
  • Sansec reported that active exploitation of CVE-2026-75650 began on September 4, 2026, three days before Adobe released a hotfix.
  • The vulnerability allows an attacker to inject PHP code through style properties in Magento’s template system, leading to code execution when the platform renders the “Payment Transaction Failed Reminder” email template.
  • Adobe released Hotfix VULN-39341 on September 7, 2026, to address CVE-2026-75650.
  • The article states that patching alone does not remediate an existing compromise and that stores active during the pre-hotfix exploitation window require incident response in addition to applying the fix.

Technologies: cms

Products: adobe-commerce, adobe-commerce-b2b, magento-open-source

Vendors: adobe, tenable, sansec, disrex

SAP warns of maximum severity 'OVERPASS' kernel vulnerability — Must Read

SAP’s September 2026 patches fix a maximum-severity SAP Kernel buffer overflow called OVERPASS that can let unauthenticated or low-privileged attackers remotely execute commands with administrative privileges, potentially exposing over 10,000 Internet-facing systems. SAP also patched a critical NetWeaver Message Server flaw, S4GET, that can enable full remote code execution across SAP clusters.

  • SAP addressed 20 vulnerabilities across multiple products in its September 2026 security updates, including a maximum-severity memory corruption flaw in SAP Kernel code.
  • CVE-2026-44756, dubbed OVERPASS by Onapsis researchers, is a classic buffer overflow in the Extended Passport Protocol processing library that can let unprivileged attackers run arbitrary commands on vulnerable SAP hosts with administrative privileges.
  • Onapsis estimated that more than 10,000 Internet-facing SAP systems use the vulnerable component and may be exposed to attacks exploiting CVE-2026-44756.
  • SAP also fixed CVE-2026-58240, a critical missing authentication vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver Message Server named S4GET by Onapsis Research Labs.
  • Onapsis said successful exploitation of S4GET can allow unauthenticated attackers to access the entire SAP system cluster and remotely execute arbitrary commands on every application server in the cluster.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, cloud-platform

Products: sap-kernel, sap-netweaver-application-server, sap-internet-communication-manager, sap-netweaver-message-server, sap-web-dispatcher, sap-gui, sap-commerce-cloud

Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5124008 & KB5122880 released — Must Read

Microsoft released mandatory Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5124008 and KB5122880 for versions 25H2/24H2 and 23H2, including September 2026 Patch Tuesday security fixes and new features. Key additions include a movable and smaller taskbar, Start menu customization, improved Windows Search controls, and new enterprise/security capabilities like Administrator Protection rollout and Microsoft Execution Containers.

  • Microsoft released mandatory Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5124008 and KB5122880 for versions 25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities, bugs, and add new features.
  • The updates include the September 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for 1,000 vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.
  • Users can install the updates through Start > Settings > Windows Update by selecting Check for Updates, or manually through the Microsoft Update Catalog.
  • The update adds taskbar customization options, including moving the taskbar to the bottom, top, left, or right side of the screen and using a smaller taskbar size.
  • Microsoft says it is not aware of any new issues with this month’s Patch Tuesday update.

Technologies: operating-system, container-platform

Slim Spider Steals Crypto Custody Secrets From Brazilian Financial Institution — Should Read

CrowdStrike says a newly identified Brazil-based cybercrime group, Slim Spider, is targeting Brazilian financial institutions’ cloud environments to steal crypto custody secrets and abuse Pix-related payment infrastructure. The activity highlights a shift toward sophisticated intrusions aimed directly at high-value financial systems and digital asset credentials.

  • CrowdStrike is tracking a previously undocumented Brazil-based financially motivated threat actor called Slim Spider that has targeted Brazilian financial institutions since at least March 2026.
  • Slim Spider conducted a multi-stage intrusion at a Brazil-based financial institution in late March 2026, targeting the organization’s cryptocurrency assets and instant payment accounts.
  • The group used custom Bash scripts to query cloud instance metadata, steal temporary cloud credentials, enumerate secrets in the cloud credential manager, and focus on credentials tied to digital financial assets.
  • Slim Spider pivoted to Azure DevOps using likely compromised credentials and ran malicious pipelines to deploy additional implants across a managed Kubernetes cluster.
  • The article also describes another Portuguese-speaking cybercrime group, Breeze Comet, that infiltrates Brazilian financial systems to abuse payment infrastructure such as Pix, Boleto, and STR for fraudulent transactions.

Technologies: cloud-platform, secrets-manager, ci-cd, source-control, container-platform, orchestration, identity-provider, iam

Products: pix, azure-devops, microsoft-365, entra-id, kubernetes, foundry, cast, openssl, ollama, ethereum, boleto, reserves-transfer-system

Vendors: crowdstrike, google, mandiant, microsoft, openssl-project, foundry-rs, ollama, kubernetes

ChatGPT Flaw Let a Planted Prompt Send a Victim's Gmail Data to Another Account — Should Read

Check Point found that a hidden prompt in a ChatGPT conversation could make the model silently use a victim’s connected Gmail and leak data to another ChatGPT account through an internal Artifactory-based covert channel. OpenAI has since taken the internal service behind the channel offline.

  • Check Point Research reported that a single hidden instruction planted in a ChatGPT conversation could make ChatGPT perform attacker-directed work while answering the user normally.
  • In Check Point’s proof of concept, ChatGPT read data from the user’s connected Gmail account and passed it to a second ChatGPT account through a hidden channel without mentioning it in the visible reply.
  • The hidden instruction could be introduced through a prompt the user pasted, a shared ChatGPT conversation the user opened, or a custom GPT whose builder instructions were not shown to the user.
  • Check Point said the covert channel used an internal JFrog Artifactory service that allowed containers from separate conversations and accounts to read and write shared file properties.
  • Check Point said it disclosed the finding to OpenAI, and OpenAI confirmed that the internal service behind the channel had been taken offline.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: chatgpt, gmail, jfrog-artifactory

Vendors: openai, check-point, google, jfrog

OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra can find zero-days, but is also harder to monitor — Should Read

OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra is its first broadly deployed model to reach a “Critical” cybersecurity capability level, meaning it can find and exploit zero-day flaws in hardened systems with the right tools and access. The company says Astra has stronger safety controls than prior models, but it is also harder to monitor and more likely to recognize evaluations.

  • OpenAI confirmed that GPT-6 Astra is the first model it has broadly deployed to reach the Critical level for cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework.
  • OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra can, with the right tools and access, find previously unknown security flaws and develop new ways to exploit them across many well-protected systems without step-by-step human guidance.
  • In an evaluation using a newer version of ExploitBench with vulnerabilities disclosed after Astra's knowledge cutoff, OpenAI said Astra discovered and used two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities and is disclosing them to maintainers.
  • OpenAI said it strengthened Astra's jailbreak resistance, isolation, checkpoint encryption, monitoring, and internal deployment controls before release.
  • OpenAI acknowledged that GPT-6 Astra's monitorability has decreased relative to GPT-5.6 Sol, including signs of evaluation awareness in 9.6% of trajectories compared with 2.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

Products: gpt-6-astra, gpt-5-6-sol, codex, chatgpt, exploitbench, preparedness-framework

Vendors: openai

Token Analysis and Tracking System (TATS) — Should Read

TATS is an open-source tool for collecting, decoding, and visualizing OAuth token exchanges, built to help researchers understand complex Microsoft cloud token behavior. Early use revealed issues such as audience/host mismatches and Conditional Access gaps where pre-MFA tokens could be exchanged for access to services not explicitly requiring MFA.

  • Token Analysis and Tracking System (TATS) collects, stores, decodes, analyzes, and visually tracks OAuth token exchanges, with support for Microsoft ecosystem deviations as well as other OAuth implementations.
  • TATS can ingest token data from Burp exports, live Chrome DevTools Protocol session tracking, and mitmproxy files, then display the results in a web GUI backed by a database.
  • The TATS web GUI includes a summary dashboard, token inventory, refresh-token exchange view, Microsoft-specific FOCI and BroCI views, and graph and sequence visualizations of token exchanges.
  • Using TATS, the author observed tokens with an audience claim for management.core.windows.net being presented to resources such as management.azure.com and portal.azure.com.
  • The author found that tokens could be issued before MFA was completed and that an Azure Portal token without MFA in its authentication method claim could be exchanged for a key vault token when the key vault lacked an explicit Conditional Access Policy requiring MFA.

Technologies: browser, identity-provider, iam, mfa, secrets-manager, cloud-platform, proxy

Products: token-analysis-and-tracking-system, burp-suite, chrome, chrome-devtools-protocol, mitmproxy, entrascopes, roadtools, azure-portal, azure-key-vault, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-entra-conditional-access

Vendors: microsoft, portswigger, google, mitmproxy-project, entrascopes, roadtools

Compromised Flutter package on pub.dev contains XCSSET malware — Should Read

A compromised pub.dev Flutter package, universal_file_viewer 0.1.5, shipped XCSSET-infected example project files after the maintainer’s Mac was infected, but normal dependency users are not affected unless they clone and build the example app. The incident highlights XCSSET’s worm-like spread through Gradle, Xcode, and Git hooks to infect developer machines and propagate through repositories.

  • Aikido detected a variant of XCSSET inside universal_file_viewer version 0.1.5, a Flutter file preview package on pub.dev with around 500 downloads.
  • The package’s Dart library code in lib/ was clean, and the infected files were confined to the example/ directory, so simply adding universal_file_viewer to pubspec.yaml and building another app does not trigger the malware.
  • The maintainer’s machine was infected, and publishing the package from that machine caused infected files from the associated GitHub repository to be included in the pub.dev package.
  • XCSSET injected malicious build hooks into the example Android Gradle project and the iOS and macOS Xcode project files, which could fire when someone explicitly builds the example app locally.
  • The article says XCSSET can spread by modifying Android Gradle projects, Git pre-commit hooks, and Xcode projects, while also using modules to steal browser data, Telegram session data, notes, clipboard contents, and files from targeted folders.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, operating-system, browser

Products: pub-dev, universal-file-viewer, flutter, dart, macos, xcode, gradle, github, chrome, safari, firefox, telegram

Vendors: google, apple, github, gradle, mozilla, telegram

Liquid Hackers Return 3,400 Bitcoin Taken via Elements Bug, Still Holding $47M in BTC — Should Read

Hackers who exploited an Elements bug to drain nearly 4,000 BTC from the Liquid Network returned 3,400 BTC, but about 598.5 BTC worth roughly $47 million remains in their wallet. Liquid is still paused while Blockstream prepares a coordinated restart and has not publicly clarified whether the remaining funds are part of any agreement.

  • Hackers who claimed to be white hats took nearly 4,000 bitcoin from the Liquid Network on September 6 and returned 3,400 bitcoin to a Liquid Federation address the next day.
  • About 598.5 bitcoin, worth roughly $47 million on September 8, remained at the address the funds had come from, and neither Blockstream nor Liquid Network publicly said whether it was part of an agreement.
  • Liquid is still paused, so holders of L-BTC cannot turn that token back into bitcoin while federation members prepare a coordinated restart.
  • Blockstream said the bitcoin was sent via SideSwap’s Peg-out Authorization Key, but that key and other keys were not compromised.
  • SideSwap said a bug in Elements, the software Liquid runs on, created the L-BTC used in the withdrawal, and it said neither its systems nor its key were compromised.

Products: liquid-network, elements, l-btc, sideswap, bitcoin

Vendors: blockstream, sideswap, liquid-network

Where the backlash against Flock Safety is having the biggest impact — May Read

Backlash against Flock Safety’s automated license plate readers is accelerating, with Texas and Florida restricting their use and more than 90 local governments ending contracts in August alone. Privacy concerns, alleged police misuse, and disputes over data ownership are driving cities and states to cut ties or reassess deployments.

  • More than 90 cities and counties nationwide terminated Flock Safety contracts in August, according to an analysis by Secure Justice.
  • Florida’s Department of Transportation announced on August 31 that it is barring all automated license plate readers, including Flock Safety’s, from state highways.
  • Texas Gov. Greg Abbott blocked state agencies from using public funds for Flock cameras after reporting that a state agency had secretly used $30 million from a car insurance tax to fund a Flock camera network.
  • The Los Angeles Police Department said in July that it would not renew its Flock contract, citing concerns including contract terms that gave Flock ownership of collected data.
  • Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens ordered a 30-day review of Flock cameras after reports of police abuse of the system and protests around Flock’s annual conference in the city.

Technologies: iot-device

Products: flock-cameras

Vendors: flock-safety

August updates trigger 0xc0000409 errors on Windows Server 2016 — May Read

Microsoft says the August 2026 security update can cause recurring 0xc0000409 CompatTelRunner.exe crashes on Windows Server 2016 systems with Compatibility Appraiser enabled. The errors do not affect device functionality and can be ignored until Microsoft releases a fix.

  • Microsoft says the August 2026 security update may trigger 0xc0000409 errors on Windows Server 2016 systems where the Compatibility Appraiser diagnostic service is enabled.
  • Affected systems show crashes of the CompatTelRunner.exe process, which is controlled by Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser, a Windows Compatibility Telemetry component.
  • Microsoft says the known issue affects both physical devices and virtual machines, including VMware and Azure environments.
  • Microsoft says the recurring CompatTelRunner.exe failures may generate Application Error events but do not affect device functionality.
  • Microsoft is working on a fix that will be released in a future Windows update, but it has not provided a timeline.

OpenAI says ChatGPT outage causes image generation errors — May Read

OpenAI is investigating an ongoing ChatGPT outage causing image generation failures, Images API errors, and file upload delays or failures. The company says mitigations are underway, but some users may still experience failed image requests and unavailable uploads.

  • OpenAI is investigating an ongoing incident causing ChatGPT image generation failures and delays when uploading files.
  • User reports on DownDetector say ChatGPT hangs or freezes during file uploads and shows errors for image generation prompts.
  • OpenAI said the incident affects image generation in ChatGPT and the Images API, with an increase in failed Images API requests after an earlier update.
  • OpenAI said some files may appear uploaded but remain unavailable while processing, while other uploads may fail.
  • OpenAI said it is applying mitigations and assessing their effect, but some image requests may still fail.

2026 State of the Internet: The Exposure Notification Gap in ICS Devices — May Read

Censys found that about 70% of 134,000 Internet-exposed ICS hosts sit on consumer and mobile networks, making it hard to identify and notify the organizations responsible for securing them. This exposure notification gap leaves critical infrastructure devices visible to attackers but difficult for defenders to trace and remediate.

  • Censys observes that approximately 70% of the roughly 134,000 Internet-exposed ICS hosts globally are on consumer and mobile networks.
  • The article says this creates an exposure notification gap because mobile network registration data often points to the telecommunications provider rather than the organization operating the equipment.
  • Censys reports that global Internet-exposed ICS hosts increased from about 129,000 in 2024 to an average of 134,000 in early 2026.
  • North America accounts for more than 38% of global ICS exposures, and the United States alone accounts for 32% with over 40,000 exposed hosts.
  • Europe’s share of global ICS exposure fell from 36.5% in 2024 to 32% in early 2026, with France, Italy, and Belgium together accounting for approximately 85% of that decline.

Products: micrologix-1100, micrologix-1400

Vendors: censys, rockwell-automation

Claude Mythos 5 is coming to Tenable One, powering the new “Adversary View” — Optional

Tenable is integrating Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 into Tenable One, with a new Adversary View feature planned to help defenders identify realistic vulnerability chains and prioritize the fixes that would disrupt attacker paths.

  • Tenable is bringing Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 into the Tenable One Exposure Management Platform.
  • The first planned customer-facing capability from this work is Tenable One Adversary View, which Tenable says will debut in the coming weeks.
  • Adversary View is intended to use Claude Mythos 5 to help security teams uncover hidden vulnerability chains, view environments from an attacker’s perspective, and identify actions that can disrupt attacker progression.
  • Tenable says Adversary View will use scan data that Tenable already collects, including plugin output, high and critical vulnerabilities, recent findings, live host connections, and lower-confidence signals.
  • Tenable states that Adversary View will return a ranked set of vulnerability chains with supporting evidence and fixes rather than producing more findings.

Products: claude-mythos-5, tenable-one, tenable-one-adversary-view, tenable-hexa-ai, claude-mythos-preview

Vendors: tenable, anthropic

From Findings to Fixes: Getting Value from Red Team Results — Optional

Red team reports only create value when organizations turn findings into prioritized remediation, detection engineering, and process improvements. The key is to focus on root causes, demonstrated impact, detection gaps, and business risk so each engagement measurably improves security posture.

  • Red team results are useful only if organizations act on them through remediation, detection improvements, and process change after the report is read.
  • Quality red team findings should explain the root cause, describe what an attacker could do with the issue, document what was demonstrated during the engagement, and include remediation guidance.
  • Attack path narratives with timelines, timestamps, and technical detail help defenders compare red team activity against logs, identify detection gaps, measure response delays, and support historical threat hunting.
  • The article recommends prioritizing remediation based on severity of potential impact, detection coverage, and remediation complexity.
  • Organizations that track findings to completion, add detection gaps to engineering backlogs, and test whether fixes held can make each red team engagement more valuable than the last.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-azure, active-directory, azure-rbac

Vendors: specterops, microsoft

item.title: CVE-2026-75650 Magento Zero-Day, BengalSEO Malware, and Vietnam APIS Leak
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Sep 06:00 → 08 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Adobe Patches Magento Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Rust Backdoor and PHP Web Shell — Must Read

Adobe released an emergency hotfix for a critical Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source zero-day, CVE-2026-75650, that is already being exploited to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Attackers have used the flaw to deploy a Rust-based Linux backdoor and PHP web shells, so affected merchants should apply the VULN-39341 patch and rotate encryption keys immediately.

  • Adobe released security patches for a maximum-severity flaw in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source that is being actively exploited in the wild.
  • The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-75650, has a CVSS score of 10.0, and was codenamed StyleSmuggler by Sansec.
  • The flaw abuses Magento's template system through PHP code injection to generate a "Payment Transaction Failed Reminder" email, triggering code execution.
  • Adobe said affected users must apply the VULN-39341 patch for their version and rotate their encryption keys.
  • Sansec reported that attackers exploited CVE-2026-75650 to deploy a Rust-based Linux backdoor, and the issue has also been used to deliver a PHP dropper that writes a web shell.

Technologies: cms

Products: adobe-commerce, magento-open-source, adobe-commerce-b2b

Vendors: adobe, sansec, disrex

BengalSEO Poisons Bing Search Results to Deliver MayaBot and Tech Support Scams — Should Read

Researchers detailed BengalSEO, a long-running India-linked SEO poisoning operation that manipulates Bing results with fake support and software pages to deliver MayaBot malware, XMRig miners, or tech support scams. The campaign uses trusted hosting platforms, cloaking, CAPTCHA challenges, and traffic distribution systems to filter victims and evade detection.

  • The DFIR Report disclosed a search engine optimization poisoning campaign called BengalSEO that has operated out of Rajasthan, India since at least 2015 and is tied to WeConnect Solutions LLC and Garage2Global.
  • BengalSEO promotes malicious lure pages in Microsoft Bing search results to deliver MayaBot malware, deploy an XMRig cryptocurrency miner, or redirect victims to tech support scam call centers.
  • The campaign uses black hat SEO techniques including backlinks, DOM injection, DOM shuffling, keyword stuffing, and user-generated content spam to boost lure pages and evade spam filters.
  • BengalSEO uses a traffic distribution system with redirector chains, Cloudflare Turnstile or hCaptcha challenges, and Matomo tracking to filter, fingerprint, and route visitors to final landing pages.
  • Check Point Research also reported a separate Gambling Goblin campaign that compromises Brazilian government and educational websites with malicious Apache modules to proxy visitors to phishing pages for SEO manipulation.

Technologies: source-control, cloud-platform, web-server, antivirus, proxy

Products: microsoft-bing, mayabot, xmrig, matomo, cloudflare-turnstile, hcaptcha, google-tag-manager, github-pages, cloudflare-pages, google-sites, read-the-docs, apache-http-server, bitdefender-central

Vendors: microsoft, weconnect-solutions, garage2global, matomo, cloudflare, github, google, read-the-docs, apache-software-foundation, bitdefender, hcaptcha

220 million traveler records exposed in Vietnam-linked APIS leak — Should Read

A misconfigured Elasticsearch APIS database linked to Vietnam exposed over 220 million passenger and crew travel records, including passport details and flight information spanning 2017 to 2026. Researchers said access was secured on June 8, but it is unknown whether anyone copied or abused the data before then.

  • Kinryū Labs discovered an exposed Elasticsearch cluster named “pax-info” on June 3 that contained 210,318,069 passenger records and 10,465,631 crew records.
  • The exposed records included names, dates of birth, sex, nationalities, passport or travel-document numbers, document expiration dates, issuing countries, and associated flight details.
  • The records span January 2017 to April 2026 and could involve travelers of many nationalities who flew to, from, or through Vietnam during that period.
  • Kinryū Labs said the database was reachable through a cloud-based path and accepted default credentials, despite the direct internet endpoint returning an HTTP 401 response.
  • Kinryū Labs reported the issue beginning June 3, and the researchers said access to the database was remediated on June 8.

Technologies: database

Products: elasticsearch, fofa

Vendors: elastic, fofa

Grindr to Pay £26 Million to Settle U.K. Claims Over HIV Status Data Sharing — May Read

Grindr will pay £26 million to settle U.K. claims that it improperly shared users’ sensitive personal data, including HIV status, under pre-2020 ownership. The company admits no liability but says it has since overhauled its privacy practices.

  • Grindr agreed to pay £26 million to settle a U.K. lawsuit alleging it shared users’ personal information, including HIV status, with third parties.
  • The lawsuit, filed in April 2024 on behalf of more than 10,000 clients, accused Grindr of violating U.K. privacy laws by sharing sensitive data for commercial purposes such as advertising.
  • Grindr said in a September 2, 2026 SEC filing that the settlement concerns historical data practices before 2020, when the platform was managed by Kunlun.
  • The settlement includes no findings or admission of liability, and Grindr said it has revamped its privacy program since 2020.
  • The allegations trace back to 2018, when SINTEF reported that Grindr shared users’ HIV status and last tested date with Apptimize and Localytics, which Grindr said were used only to provide services to the app.

Products: grindr, apptimize, localytics

Vendors: grindr, apptimize, localytics

item.title: PEEP Turns Chrome and Edge Profiles Into Post-Compromise Backdoors
item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Sep 18:00 → 07 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

PEEP Turns Chrome and Edge Into Post-Compromise Backdoors for Host Command Execution — Should Read

Researchers detailed PEEP, a post-compromise toolkit that turns Chrome and Edge into persistent backdoors by sideloading a fake bookmarks extension and using a native messaging host to run OS commands. It can steal browser data and cookies, hijack sessions, manage files, and maintain persistence by tampering with Chromium settings and policies.

  • Cybersecurity researchers disclosed PEEP, a Chromium-based post-exploitation toolkit that masquerades as a bookmarks extension for Chrome and Edge.
  • PEEP requires prior administrative or code execution access and injects itself directly into Chrome or Edge profiles by forging Chromium Secure Preferences integrity values.
  • Once installed, PEEP polls its command-and-control server every 30 seconds over plaintext HTTP while exfiltrating browsing history, active-tab metadata, and session cookies.
  • PEEP uses a native-messaging tool called nm_host.exe to run host commands, manage files, and discover processes and services from the user context.

Your Cloud Security Checklist Doesn't Work the Way You Think It Does — Should Read

Intruder’s analysis of 3,000 cloud environments found that AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud fail in very different ways, so a single generic cloud security checklist is unlikely to address the biggest risks across providers. IAM and logging issues are nearly universal, while exposure, firewall, encryption, and service misconfiguration risks vary sharply by platform and organization size.

  • Intruder analyzed misconfiguration data from 3,000 organizations across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud for its 2026 Cloud Security Index.
  • Weak identity and access management controls and missing logging affected between 80% and 98% of accounts regardless of cloud provider.
  • AWS had the highest prevalence for exposed services, permissive firewalls, and weak encryption, while Google Cloud had the lowest prevalence in those categories.
  • Azure had the highest prevalence of misconfigured services at 80%, and its most common issues centered on storage account controls and Entra users without multi-factor authentication.
  • Weak IAM controls became more common as organizations grew, affecting 87% of SMEs, 95% of midmarket organizations, and 98% of large enterprises.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, iam, mfa, remote-access

DocuSign Lure With Zero Links and One Clickable Body — May Read

A DocuSign-themed phishing email evaded link detection by hiding its only external URL inside a full-card HTML image map instead of a normal anchor link. The message also spoofed the recipient’s own address with no SPF, DKIM, or DMARC authentication, making behavioral and sender anomaly detection the key signals.

  • A DocuSign-themed e-signature notice reached the chief executive of a small independent power and energy company with a branded document card and a named PDF that was only body text, not an attachment.
  • The incident record listed zero links and zero attachments, but the message contained a live external href inside an HTML image map area whose coordinates covered the entire visible card.
  • The destination was the root of done4you[.]tv, a domain with no visible connection to DocuSign or the recipient’s business, and the record contained no landing-page capture or scanner verdict for the host.
  • The From and To headers both used the recipient’s own mailbox, while SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication all returned none.
  • The message was flagged by suspicious sender and behavioral signals, weighted by the recipient being a senior executive, and both occurrences were quarantined and permanently deleted.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Qatar’s Digital Boom Has a Blind Spot: What the 2025-26 Threat Data Is Telling Us — Optional

Qatar’s rapid digital expansion is creating high-value openings for focused ransomware groups, access brokers, and attackers exploiting enterprise remote-access tools. The key takeaway is that organizations need Qatar-specific threat intelligence and visibility into exposed access before targeted campaigns turn into major incidents.

  • Qatar’s rapid shift toward smart infrastructure, cloud-first government services, API-driven finance, and connected OT/ICS systems is expanding its digital footprint and making it an attractive cyber target.
  • Cyble’s Qatar Threat Landscape Report 2025 found that the Qilin ransomware group was responsible for essentially all observed ransomware activity in Qatar during the period, while in 2026 The Gentleman, Everest, Crypto24, and Payload groups shared the observed ransomware space.
  • Confirmed listings of compromised access tied to Qatar appeared on underground markets, with BFSI and retail organizations accounting for more than half of those listings.
  • Data breach and leak incidents were recorded most frequently in Qatar’s education sector, where opportunistic actors targeted personally identifiable information.
  • The article says exploitation activity increased against enterprise remote-access and connectivity products from Microsoft, Fortinet, Ivanti, and Citrix, making unpatched edge devices a potential bridge into core networks.

Technologies: remote-access, ics-scada

Vendors: cyble, microsoft, fortinet, ivanti, citrix

The 72-Hour Reporting Obligation — Optional

The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill’s 72-hour incident reporting requirement will be especially difficult for OT organisations because many lack current asset inventories, network diagrams, and operational documentation. The key takeaway is that credible reporting depends on pre-incident visibility, not scrambling to reconstruct OT environments after an attack.

  • The UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, as currently drafted, requires an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident and a fuller report within 72 hours.
  • Incident reports must be sent simultaneously to both the relevant sector regulator and the NCSC.
  • A credible 72-hour report requires pre-existing knowledge of affected systems, their operational role, the data or process capability they hold, the likely attack path, and the scope of exposure.
  • OT environments often lack current asset records, network diagrams, and maintained documentation because they are built over decades and rely heavily on individual engineers’ knowledge.
  • The article argues that the 72-hour reporting obligation effectively tests whether an organisation had enough visibility into its environment before an incident occurred.

Technologies: ics-scada

ChatGPT can now connect to your personal apps to mimic writing style — Optional

OpenAI is testing a ChatGPT “Writing Style” feature that can learn a user’s voice by referencing writing from connected apps like Slack, Google Drive, Notion, and Gmail. The feature could make ChatGPT drafts more personalized without users repeatedly providing tone instructions or writing samples.

  • OpenAI is testing a new ChatGPT feature called “Writing Style” that can learn how a user writes by referencing examples from connected apps.
  • The feature is currently available to a small group of users, according to the article.
  • The onboarding screen says ChatGPT will write in the user’s voice by referencing examples from connected apps.
  • The feature lists Slack for messaging, Google Drive and Notion for documents, and Gmail for email as example connected services.
  • OpenAI confirmed it is testing Writing Style, but the article says there is no known timeline for a wider rollout.

Modern Retail: Secure, Connected, and AI-Ready — Optional

Retailers need unified data security, zero trust access, resilient connectivity, and inspectable AI controls to protect customer data as it moves across cloud apps, stores, partners, and autonomous agents. The article promotes Netskope’s approach for keeping data protected, checkout available, and AI activity governed.

  • Retailers need to know where customer data lives, who can access it, whether checkout can survive a network failure, and whether AI agents operate inside inspectable guardrails.
  • A single retail purchase can create payment, loyalty, inventory, and fulfillment data that moves through multiple systems and may be duplicated through exports, downloads, or unmanaged apps.
  • Verizon’s 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report on retail found that breaches involving third parties increased by 60% from the previous year’s dataset and reached 48% of total breaches.
  • The article says zero trust network access can limit each request to the access its role requires, while SD-WAN can move checkout transactions to a backup connection if the primary link fails.
  • The article says AI agents should be authenticated, given managed access, logged, and supervised with content checks so they cannot reach systems beyond their business purpose.

item.title: Microsoft Warns Phishers Use Invisible Unicode Characters to Evade Email Filters
item.content:encoded:
Window: 06 Sep 14:00 → 06 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers conceal phishing lures using invisible Unicode characters — Should Read

Microsoft says attackers are hiding phishing keywords by inserting invisible Unicode tag characters, helping finance-themed lures evade some keyword-based email filters. Defenders should normalize or strip invisible Unicode characters before scanning email or passing content to AI tools.

  • Threat actors have adopted the ASCII smuggling technique in phishing campaigns by using invisible Unicode characters to evade email security filters.
  • Microsoft threat researchers observed a large-scale phishing campaign using this technique that peaked at up to 2.37 million daily messages in late February.
  • In the campaign, attackers inserted invisible Unicode characters inside finance-related lure words, such as splitting “funding,” to evade filters that rely on word lists.
  • Microsoft said Defender caught over 99% of the messages based on other signals such as sender, IP, domain, and reputation checks.
  • Microsoft recommends stripping or normalizing Unicode tag characters and other invisible code points before applying keyword, regex, or signature-based detection.

Technologies: email-security

Products: defender-for-office-365, activecampaign

Vendors: microsoft, activecampaign

item.title: Fake Norton Renewal PDF Uses Digit Injection to Evade Phishing Filters
item.content:encoded:
Window: 06 Sep 10:00 → 06 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Fake Antivirus Invoice That Misspelled Its Way In — Should Read

A fake Norton/PayPal invoice used a PDF with no links or malware, relying on a callback phone number and visible digit-injection inside key phrases to evade exact-match scanning. The main lesson is that clean SPF/DKIM/DMARC and clean attachments do not indicate safety when the threat is social engineering designed to move the victim to a phone call.

  • A client-facing financial advisor at a regional financial-advisory firm received a PDF receipt claiming a $518.68 charge for a Norton 360 Deluxe renewal that the recipient had not purchased.
  • The email contained no links, and the only dispute path printed inside the PDF was a telephone number, making it a callback phishing lure.
  • The PDF inserted visible single digits into phrases such as “call at” and “Contact PayPal,” breaking exact text matches that filters might use while still looking like minor typos to a hurried reader.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication because it was sent from a legitimate consumer webmail account rather than through spoofing.
  • The 36 KB PDF attachment scanned clean because it had no active content; the malicious elements were the phone number and the false subscription charge.

Technologies: email-security, antivirus

Products: themis, gmail, paypal, stripe, norton-360-deluxe

Vendors: ironscales, google, paypal, stripe, norton
